title: Withdraw the slide board from under the patient: one hand steadies, the other pulls
instruction: Pull the blue slide board out from under the pink patient block and leave it lying on the white bed deck, with the patient block resting flat on the deck where it is. Steady the block with the other gripper while you pull: it must not be dragged, pushed or carried more than 15 mm, lifted more than 3 cm, tipped, or dropped. Let go of both at the end.
context: After a lateral transfer onto a bed, the slide (transfer) board is withdrawn from under the patient. Safe patient handling practice has two carers for this: one steadies the patient, holding the torso or taking a little of its weight, while the other withdraws the board, because pulling the board with the patient's weight on it drags the patient with it (shear on the skin, pressure injury, a slide toward the bed's edge), and the patient is never lifted away or let drop. Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131), orderlies (31-1132) and registered nurses (29-1141) do this many times a shift. Here a weighted block stands in for the patient's torso on a board lying on a bed deck: pulling the board drags the block unless the block is held, so the job needs both arms by physics, and the rules about the block (never moved, lifted, tipped or dropped) are checked at every moment of the trial, not only at the end. A robot that finishes the job by any route that moves the patient scores nothing.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Three things are on the table. (1) Bed deck: a fixed white rigid platform (painted plywood) standing in for the mattress surface, 200 mm along x, 440 mm along y, 30 mm tall, centred at x 28.0 cm, y -4.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y (it spans x 18..38 cm, y -26..+18 cm); its top is 30 mm above the table. (2) Slide board: a loose light-blue hollow polymer transfer board, 40 mm wide (along x), 320 mm long (along y), 20 mm thick, 0.10 kg, lying flat on the deck centred at x 28.0 cm, y +2.0 cm, long side along y (it spans y -14..+18 cm, its left end at the deck's left edge). (3) Patient: a loose skin-pink plastic block, weighted, standing in for the patient's torso, 70 mm along x, 60 mm along y, 40 mm tall, 0.20 kg, lying flat on the board centred at x 28.0 cm, y +10.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y (its underside 20 mm above the deck; it overhangs the 40 mm board by 15 mm on each side in x; the board runs 50 mm beyond it toward the left and 210 mm toward the right). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step (20 Hz) it reads the patient's and the board's poses and velocities and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the fingers 94 mm apart). Patient rules, at every moment: 'moved' is the horizontal distance of the patient's centre from where it lay at the trial's first step; 'raised' is the height of the centre of its underside above the board's top (where it started); 'tilt' is the angle of its vertical axis from the vertical; 'descent' is its downward speed (the larger of its reported speed and how far its underside came down in that control step, divided by the step). Score 0 if at any moment moved exceeds 15 mm, raised exceeds 30 mm, tilt exceeds 10 degrees, descent exceeds 0.15 m/s, or the patient or the board is off the table (lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top); and 0 if at the end the patient's centre is not over the deck. Board progress is read from the two outlines seen from above (world-aligned bounding boxes): 'still under' is the share of the board's starting footprint under the patient (40 x 60 mm) that is still under it; 'fully out' means the outlines do not overlap and are at least 10 mm apart; 'pulled' is how far the board's centre has gone along -y (toward the right) from where it lay. 'Resting flat on the deck' means the lowest point is within 3 mm of the deck's top and the centre is over the deck, tilted less than 3 degrees for the board (either broad face up) and less than 5 degrees for the patient. A gripper has 'let go' of its item (the left the patient, the right the board) when its opening is 0.9 or more (fingers at least 84.5 mm apart) or its fingers' zone (every point within the fingers' outer-corner radius of the segment from the finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper) is more than 10 mm from that item. Otherwise, at the last step: 1.0 if the board is fully out and resting flat on the deck, the patient is resting flat on the deck, and both grippers have let go; 0.75 if the board is fully out and the patient is resting flat on the deck, but a gripper still holds or the board is not resting flat on the deck (hanging over the deck's edge, tilted, held up); 0.5 if no more than half of the board's starting footprint under the patient is still under it (a straight pull of at least 80 mm, since the board starts 50 mm past the patient); 0.25 if the board has been pulled at least 20 mm along its length but more than half is still under; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both objects still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, 'both grippers let go' is taken as met. In a real trial, tape the patient block's outline and a second outline 15 mm outside it on the deck, stand a card upright behind the block with marks at 30 mm above the board's top, and film from the side and from above: the moved and raise limits are read against the tape and the card, the tilt and the set-down against the side video, and 'fully out' and 'half out' against the block's taped outline.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) between every pair of surfaces, which is what makes the board drag the block. The patient is a uniform rigid block (a real torso is soft, heavy and conforms to the board), the board a rigid solid box of the stated mass, and the bed deck a fixed hard platform (a real mattress yields). The arm's controller does not carry a payload's weight, so a held block sags a few millimetres below its commanded height. Gripper heading is not read, so each finger zone is round, wider than the real fingers across their closing direction. The scorer cannot tell a block held perfectly still within 3 mm of the deck from one resting on it; the 3 s stillness with both grippers let go covers that.
reset_notes: Put the board back flat on the deck centred at x 28.0 cm, y +2.0 cm, long side along y, and the patient block back flat on the board centred at x 28.0 cm, y +10.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. Nothing is consumed.
